nodes.summary: Approximation and interpolation of functions: Chebyshev equioscillation, best approximation, Lagrange interpolation, Bernstein polynomials and Voronovskaya, Korovkin, Müntz–Szász, Runge, Kolmogorov superposition, universal approximation.
nodes.title: Approximation theory

nodes.summary: Asymptotic expansions and methods: Euler–Maclaurin and Watson's lemma, Laplace-type integrals, coefficient asymptotics of power series (Bender's lemma), Stirling-type and inverse-factorial expansions, and asymptotic expansions of power sums, Lambert series and log sums; complex-analytic saddle-point results on entire functions go to Complex analysis.
nodes.title: Asymptotic analysis

nodes.summary: Normed, Banach and topological vector spaces: duality, weak topologies, geometry of the unit ball, bases and classical sequence spaces.
nodes.title: Banach space theory

nodes.summary: Holomorphic and meromorphic functions of one and several complex variables: Cauchy theory, entire functions, conformal and univalent maps, zeros of polynomials, and Hilbert and Banach spaces of analytic functions.
nodes.title: Complex analysis

nodes.summary: Convex functions and sets in analysis and optimization: Fenchel conjugates, polar sets, Moreau decomposition, convex projections, KKT conditions, gradient descent rates, Stampacchia, Tikhonov regularization, Euler–Lagrange, mountain pass and Ekeland principles; linear programming goes to convex geometry. Ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization of a finite-dimensional least-squares problem, is under least squares,…
nodes.title: Convex analysis and calculus of variations

nodes.summary: Test functions, Schwartz functions, tempered distributions and distributional derivatives: principal values, Plemelj limits, Dirac comb, partitions of unity.
nodes.title: Distributions

nodes.summary: Fixed points of nonexpansive, Lipschitz and affine maps: the Browder–Göhde–Kirk theorem and Kirk's normal structure, Markov–Kakutani, Browder's demiclosedness principle, maps with contracting iterates.
nodes.title: Fixed-point theory

nodes.summary: L^p and Sobolev spaces of functions: embeddings (Morrey, Rellich, radial, trace), Ehrling, Agmon, Ladyzhenskaya, Gagliardo–Nirenberg and weighted Hardy–Sobolev inequalities, sup-norm bounds by H¹ energy, L^p limits and weak convergence in L^p.
nodes.title: Function spaces and Sobolev inequalities

nodes.summary: Fourier series, the Fourier transform on R^n, Fourier analysis on finite groups and the Boolean cube, singular integrals, and other integral transforms and moment problems.
nodes.title: Harmonic analysis

nodes.summary: Geometry of inner product spaces: nearest-point projections, orthonormal and Hilbert bases, separability and ℓ², frames and Riesz bases, weak convergence (Opial, Radon–Riesz), Kirszbraun extension, derivatives of the norm, representer theorems; operators on Hilbert spaces go to Operator theory, analytic RKHS to Complex analysis.
nodes.title: Hilbert spaces

nodes.summary: Classical inequalities for sums, sequences, means and integrals of real or complex numbers: Hardy, Hilbert, Carleman, Wirtinger, Opial, Landau–Kolmogorov, Hermite–Hadamard, Kantorovich and Popoviciu, power-sum and elementary log/exp bounds; inequalities stated with Sobolev norms go to Function spaces, eigenvalue inequalities to Operator theory.
nodes.title: Inequalities

nodes.summary: Algorithms with error analysis: bisection and Newton's method, Euler and Runge–Kutta methods, Galerkin and finite element estimates (Céa, Aubin–Nitsche, Strang, Banach–Nečas–Babuška).
nodes.title: Numerical analysis

nodes.summary: Banach algebras and C*- and von Neumann algebras: exponentials and product formulas in Banach algebras, GNS, Gelfand–Naimark, bicommutant, Kaplansky density, Russo–Dye, Stinespring, Kadison–Singer and the Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava theorem.
nodes.title: Banach and operator algebras

nodes.summary: Bounded linear operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces: spectra, compact and Fredholm operators, shifts and other concrete operators, and eigenvalue inequalities.
nodes.title: Operator theory

nodes.summary: Existence and uniqueness (Cauchy–Peano, Picard, maximal solutions), linear systems and fundamental matrices, stability and Lyapunov's indirect method, Sturm–Liouville and boundary value problems with their Green's operators and eigenfunctions, oscillation and comparison theorems.
nodes.title: Ordinary differential equations

nodes.summary: PDE existence, regularity and qualitative results: Cauchy–Kovalevskaya, heat and Airy equations, Euler singularity formation, σ₂ Hessian estimates, radial symmetry, viscosity solutions, Dirichlet and Neumann spectra of the Laplacian.
nodes.title: Partial differential equations

nodes.summary: Harmonic and subharmonic functions in the plane and in R^n, harmonic conjugates, the Newton and logarithmic potentials and fundamental solutions of the Laplacian.
nodes.title: Potential theory

nodes.summary: Functions of one or several real variables: differentiation, partial derivatives and multivariable calculus, the Riemann integral and evaluation of definite integrals, continuity and pathological functions, and functional equations on the reals.
nodes.title: Real functions and calculus

nodes.summary: Convergence of numerical sequences and series and of series of functions, summability methods and Tauberian theorems, and closed-form evaluation of infinite series and products.
nodes.title: Sequences, series and summability

nodes.summary: Named transcendental functions and their series, integral representations and identities: gamma and digamma, hypergeometric functions, exponential and logarithmic integrals, Lambert W, Bessel, Dickman, Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions, and elliptic functions (elliptic-function topics sit directly in the field).
nodes.title: Special functions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
